project.name: STEImmo
project.summary: STEImmo ist eine serverseitig gerenderte Webanwendung für Vermarktung und Verwaltung einer Immobilie. Python und Django verarbeiten Anfragen; UIkit gestaltet die Oberfläche, PostgreSQL speichert Daten.

issues.detail: Wohnungsverwaltung prüfen (wohnungsverwaltung/tests.py) contains 27 secrets (a password). Anyone who can see the code can use them to get into the services they unlock as you. Treat them as leaked: move them out of the code and replace them with new ones.

For each one:
1. Replace the literal with an environment variable lookup (os.environ["NAME"] in Python), using a clear variable name. If the app can't run without it, fail with a clear error when it is missing instead of falling back to a hard-coded value.
2. Add each variable name (with an empty value, never the real one) to .env.example, and make sure .env is listed in .gitignore.
3. Update any deployment config (Docker, Cloud Run, Vercel, etc.) so the variable is set in production.
4. Run the app or its tests to confirm it still starts with the variables set.

Then give me a short checklist (without the values) of which services these keys belong to, so I can rotate each one: create a new key in that service's dashboard, put it in my environment, and revoke the old one. Because the old values are in git history, assume they are compromised.

issues.title: 4 files are very large
issues.detail: These files each have over 1,000 lines (the biggest has 3,494). AI assistants read and edit big files less reliably: they lose track of what's where and can break one part while fixing another. Splitting them into smaller files by job makes future changes safer.
issues.fix:
Refactor plan: these files are very large:
- wohnungsverwaltung/tests.py (3,494 lines)
- wohnungsverwaltung/views.py (3,159 lines)
- wohnungsverwaltung/forms.py (2,336 lines)
- wohnungsverwaltung/models.py (1,039 lines)

Start with wohnungsverwaltung/tests.py. Read it and propose how to split it into smaller files, each with one clear job (for example by feature or by type of work), keeping every public function name and behaviour the same. Show me the plan first. After I approve, move code in small steps, update the imports, and run the tests after each step. Don't change behaviour.
